introChoice.title: Self-Testing with assert
introChoice.prompt: `assert condition` is Python's built-in truth checker! If `condition` is `True`, Python quietly continues. If `condition` is `False`, Python immediately raises an `AssertionError` to alert you to a bug!
introChoice.question: What happens when `assert 2 + 2 == 5` runs?

choices.label: It prints False and then Done
choices.explanation: `assert` doesn't just print `False` — it stops execution with an `AssertionError`!

choices.label: Nothing happens — it prints Done
choices.explanation: `assert` only stays silent when the condition is `True`!

choices.label: It fixes 2 + 2 to equal 5
choices.explanation: `assert` only CHECKS whether a condition is true; it never changes math!

choices.label: It raises an AssertionError and stops
choices.explanation: Yes! Because `2 + 2 == 5` is `False`, `assert` halts right there with an `AssertionError`!

introChoice.title: Clamping a Number with min() and max()
introChoice.prompt: Clamping keeps a number safely inside a `[lo, hi]` range! `min(hi, n)` caps it so it can't go above `hi`, and `max(lo, ...)` lifts it so it can't drop below `lo`.
introChoice.question: What does `max(0, min(10, 15))` return?

choices.explanation: 15 is above `hi` (10), so `min(10, 15)` caps it down to `10`!
First `min(10, 15)` is `10`, then `max(0, 10)` picks the LARGER of 0 and 10, which is `10`!
Spot on! `min(10, 15)` caps `15` to `10`, and `max(0, 10)` keeps `10`!
`clamp()` doesn't average — it caps values to stay between `lo` (0) and `hi` (10)!
